method: The method this week was mostly talking and listening. We did popcorn-style presentations, so each person quickly shared their practice and research interests, and then we tried to connect those interests to the session themes: industries, practices, and technologies.
related_work: We finished by reading a short text together and being introduced to the Access Rider, a document where you lay out what you need to work well, whether that's about access, communication, timing, whatever. I'd never seen one before, and it made me realise how rarely this stuff gets said out loud in creative work.
conclusion_future_work: My takeaway is that the module is going to be about finding where my own interests overlap with industries, practices, and technologies. Next week I want to pin down which of those threads is actually worth chasing.
results_discussion: The popcorn presentations were the best part. Hearing everyone's practice and research interests in quick bursts gave me a much clearer sense of who's in the room and what they care about. Then connecting those interests to the themes made it click that 'industry' isn't some separate dry thing, it's just where our practices and the technologies meet. The Access Rider stuck with me too, it's such a simple idea but I can already see how it changes the way you'd set up a collaboration. I came out of the morning with a bunch of threads I want to follow.
title: Introductions, popcorn, and an Access Rider
introduction: The first session of Creative Industry Research filled a whole morning. We opened with a warm-up and introductions, then ran through the module curriculum and the organisational details. After that it got more interesting, with everyone sharing their own practice and research interests.
